q: Which redundancy option meets requirement 2 at the lowest cost?
opts: LRS
ZRS
GRS
RA-GRS
exp: Only the RA- options let you read the secondary region at any time without a failover. RA-GRS is cheaper than RA-GZRS. Plain GRS needs a failover before the secondary can be read.

q: Complete the plan for requirement 1.
tpl: Move blobs to [[0]] after 30 days and to [[1]] after 180 days, using [[2]].
exp: A lifecycle management rule can tier rarely used blobs to cool and then to archive, the cheapest tier for long retention. Archive is offline, which is acceptable for rarely used videos.

q: What should you give the partner studios (requirement 3)?
opts: An account SAS valid for 7 days
A service SAS for the container, linked to a stored access policy
The storage account access key
A user delegation SAS
exp: A service SAS tied to a stored access policy can be revoked on its own by changing or deleting the policy, without affecting other tokens. User delegation and account SAS cannot use stored access policies; revoking them means revoking all user delegation keys or rotating account keys, which breaks other tokens too.

q: What meets requirement 4?
opts: Object replication to a storage account in Lahore
Azure File Sync with a server endpoint on the Lahore file server and cloud tiering
Azure Data Box
Azure Storage Explorer installed on each client
exp: Azure File Sync keeps a central Azure file share and caches files on the local Windows Server. Cloud tiering keeps local disk use down, and NTFS permissions are preserved.

q: For requirement 5, answer Yes or No:
stmts: Create a private endpoint for the blob service in VNet-Prod
A service endpoint alone lets on-premises clients reach the storage account privately
Set public network access on the storage account to Disabled
A private DNS zone named privatelink.blob.core.windows.net is needed for name resolution
exp: A private endpoint gives the account a private IP that VNet and VPN-connected clients can reach. Service endpoints do not extend to on-premises. Disabling public access blocks the internet. The privatelink DNS zone resolves the account name to the private IP.

q: What meets requirement 1?
opts: Blob soft delete with 7-year retention
A time-based retention policy (immutable storage) on the container
A ReadOnly resource lock on the storage account
Blob versioning
exp: Time-based retention policies make blobs WORM (write once, read many) for the set period. Soft delete retention tops out at 365 days, and resource locks do not protect blob data.

q: Which TWO settings are required for requirement 4? Choose 2.
opts: Hierarchical namespace on both accounts
Blob versioning on both accounts
Both accounts in the same subscription
Change feed on the source account
exp: Object replication needs versioning on the source and destination accounts and change feed on the source. The accounts can be in different subscriptions and regions.

q: Complete the data protection settings for requirements 2 and 3.
tpl: Enable [[0]] so overwritten reports can be recovered, and [[1]] with 14-day retention for containers.
exp: Versioning keeps the previous content whenever a blob is overwritten. Container soft delete lets a deleted container be restored within its retention period.

q: Which role should the reporting app's managed identity get (requirement 5)?
opts: Reader on the storage account
Storage Account Contributor
Storage Blob Data Reader on the reports container
Owner on the resource group
exp: Storage Blob Data Reader grants read access to blob data. Reader and Storage Account Contributor are control-plane roles that do not grant data access by themselves.

q: What do you need for requirement 6?
opts: Infrastructure encryption only
Customer-managed keys in a key vault with soft delete and purge protection, accessed by the storage account's managed identity
Client-side encryption in the reporting app only
Microsoft-managed keys with a 90-day rotation
exp: Customer-managed keys give Northwind control over the key and the ability to revoke it. The vault needs soft delete and purge protection, and the account uses a managed identity to reach the key.

q: Complete the command so only new or changed files are uploaded each time it runs.
exp: azcopy sync compares source and destination and transfers only what changed. azcopy copy copies everything (unless you add overwrite options).

q: Complete the command for an upload-only stored access policy.
tpl:
az storage container policy create --container-name uploads \
  --name partner --permissions [[0]] --expiry 2026-12-31
exp: In a stored access policy, permissions are letters: r = read, a = add, c = create, w = write, d = delete, l = list. Create (c) and write (w) let partners upload new blobs but not read, list or delete anything, which matches upload-only access. 'rl' is read and list, and 'racwdl' is full access.

q: Choose the redundancy for each goal.
tpl:
Survive a zone outage without data leaving the region: [[0]]
Survive a region outage and read the secondary at any time: [[1]]
exp: ZRS keeps three synchronous copies across availability zones in one region, so it survives a zone outage without data leaving the region. RA-GRS copies data to the paired region and lets applications read that secondary copy at any time, so it survives a region outage. LRS stays in one datacenter, and plain GRS can't be read until failover.

q: Complete the statements about access tiers.
tpl: Rehydrating a blob from archive with Standard priority can take up to [[0]]. The early-deletion period for the cool tier is [[1]] days.
exp: Standard-priority rehydration can take up to 15 hours. Cool has a 30-day minimum, cold 90 days and archive 180 days.

q: Complete the rule so blobs in the "logs" container move to cool after 30 days and are deleted after 365 days.
exp: prefixMatch starts with the container name, such as "logs/". The delete action removes blobs after the given number of days.

q: Complete the commands so only the office public IP 203.0.113.10 can reach the account.
tpl:
az storage account update -n st1 -g RG1 --default-action [[0]]
az storage account network-rule add -n st1 -g RG1 --ip-address [[1]]
exp: Setting the default action to Deny turns on the firewall; then you allow the office's public IP. Private addresses such as 10.0.0.4 cannot be used in IP rules.

q: Complete the statement about identity-based access to Azure Files.
tpl: Share-level access is granted with [[0]], and file and folder access with [[1]].
exp: Share-level permissions use roles such as Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor. File and directory permissions use Windows ACLs. Users need both.

q: Complete the command for low-latency premium SMB file shares.
tpl:
az storage account create -n stdata01 -g RG1 -l westeurope \
  --sku [[0]] --kind [[1]]
exp: Premium file shares need a FileStorage account with a premium SKU. Premium accounts do not offer GRS.

q: Complete the statements about storage encryption.
tpl: Infrastructure (double) encryption can be enabled [[0]]. Customer-managed keys can be configured [[1]].
blanks: only when the account is created
only when the account is created
exp: Infrastructure encryption is a create-time setting. Customer-managed keys can be added to new or existing accounts.

q: Complete the statement about sync groups.
tpl: Each sync group has [[0]] cloud endpoint and [[1]] server endpoint(s).
exp: A sync group syncs one Azure file share (the cloud endpoint) with one or more server paths (server endpoints).

q: Match each requirement to the cheapest redundancy option that meets it.
items: Survive a zone failure in the region
Survive zone and region failures
Lowest cost, single datacenter
Survive a region outage with the secondary readable at any time
exp: ZRS covers zones; GZRS covers zones and regions; LRS is cheapest; RA-GRS adds read access to the secondary.

q: Match each need to the access method.
items: Most secure type of SAS
Revoke many SAS tokens at once
Time-limited access for a partner without an Entra account
Let an Azure VM app read blobs without secrets
exp: A user delegation SAS is signed with Entra credentials. A stored access policy revokes all linked SAS. A service SAS works without an Entra account. Managed identities avoid secrets.

q: Match each task to the tool.
items: Browse and manage storage in a desktop app
Keep an on-premises file server cached with Azure Files
Move 80 TB with little bandwidth
Script incremental uploads from a folder
exp: Storage Explorer is the GUI; File Sync caches shares on Windows Server; Data Box ships data physically; AzCopy scripts transfers.

q: Match each workload to the blob type.
items: VM disk (VHD)
Appending log entries
Images and documents
exp: Page blobs suit random read and write (disks), append blobs suit logs, and block blobs suit general objects.

q: Match each need to the feature.
items: WORM retention for compliance
Recover earlier content after an overwrite
Keep data indefinitely during an investigation
Recover a deleted container
exp: Time-based retention enforces WORM; versioning keeps earlier content; legal holds have no end date; container soft delete restores deleted containers.

q: Match each description to the access tier.
items: Online, cheapest storage for data kept 90+ days
Offline, must be rehydrated before reading
Frequently accessed data
Online, 30-day minimum
exp: Cold is the cheapest online tier (90 days); archive is offline (180 days); hot is for frequent access; cool has a 30-day minimum.

q: Match each description to the network option.
items: Allow one public IP range
Give the account a private IP inside your VNet
Free; sends the subnet identity to the public endpoint
exp: IP rules allow public ranges; private endpoints provide a private IP; service endpoints identify the subnet to the public endpoint.

q: Match each permission need to the Azure Files share-level role.
items: Also change NTFS permissions
Read-only over SMB
Read, write and delete over SMB
targets: Storage File Data SMB Share Reader
Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor
Storage File Data SMB Share Elevated Contributor
exp: Elevated Contributor can also change ACLs; Reader is read-only; Contributor reads, writes and deletes.

q: Review the SAS URL. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: The token allows writing the blob
The token works over plain HTTP
The token works from IP address 198.51.100.4
The token is valid on 5 November 2026
exp: sp=r is read only; spr=https requires HTTPS; sip limits callers to 203.0.113.0–203.0.113.255; the validity window (st to se) includes 5 November.

q: A block blob was last modified 120 days ago. Under this policy, which tier is it in?
opts: Hot
Cool
Archive
It has been deleted
exp: After 30 days it moves to cool and after 90 days to archive. Deletion happens only after 2,555 days (about 7 years).

q: Review the storage account properties. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: Data can be read from the secondary region at any time
Trusted Azure services such as Azure Backup can reach the account despite the firewall
Anonymous users can read a blob in a container set to "Blob" access
A client on a home internet connection can reach the account
exp: Standard_RAGRS gives read access to the secondary. bypass: AzureServices allows trusted services. allowBlobPublicAccess: false overrides container settings. The firewall denies everything except SubnetA, and there are no IP rules.

q: What does this command do?
opts: Copies all blobs in container "data" from the source account to the destination account, server to server
Downloads the blobs to the local computer and then uploads them
Moves the blobs and deletes them from the source
Creates a sync relationship that keeps running in the background
exp: Copying between two storage URLs uses server-to-server copy APIs. The source is not deleted, and the command runs once.

q: A user with ONLY the Reader role on storage account st1 runs these commands. What happens?
opts: The blobs are listed
The command fails with an authorisation error, because blob data access needs a Storage Blob Data role
The blobs are listed, but downloads fail
PowerShell uses the account key automatically
exp: -UseConnectedAccount uses Entra authorisation, which needs a data-plane role such as Storage Blob Data Reader. Reader is a control-plane role.

code:
Source:      stsrc (West Europe)
Destination: stdst (North Europe)
Rule 1:
  sourceContainer:      invoices
  destinationContainer: invoices-copy
  prefixMatch:          2026/
q: Review the object replication policy. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: The blob invoices/2026/jan.pdf is replicated
The blob invoices/2025/dec.pdf is replicated
Users can write directly to the invoices-copy container
Replication is synchronous
exp: The prefix filter limits replication to blobs starting with 2026/. Destination containers are read-only while the policy exists. Replication is asynchronous.

q: This command works from an Azure VM but fails from a laptop on a home internet connection with "System error 53". What is the most likely cause?
opts: The storage account key is wrong
The ISP or home router blocks outbound TCP port 445
Azure Files does not support Windows
The share quota is full
exp: SMB uses TCP 445, which many ISPs block. The same key works from Azure, so the credentials are fine. Use a VPN or ExpressRoute, or Azure File Sync.

q: What does this Bicep file deploy?
opts: An account that survives a zone outage, with new blobs defaulting to cool, and HTTP requests rejected
An account that copies data to the paired region
An account whose blobs default to the archive tier
An account always named exactly "stapp"
exp: Standard_ZRS spans three zones, accessTier sets the default to cool, and supportsHttpsTrafficOnly rejects HTTP. uniqueString() makes the name unique per resource group.

code:
StorageBlobLogs
| where OperationName == "DeleteBlob"
| project TimeGenerated, CallerIpAddress, Uri, AuthenticationType
q: What does this query show, and what must be configured first?
opts: Who deleted blobs, from which IP and how they authenticated; a diagnostic setting must send blob logs to the workspace
Storage capacity per container; nothing needs configuring
Blob deletions from the Activity log; nothing needs configuring
Failed sign-ins to the storage account; Entra ID P2 is required
exp: StorageBlobLogs holds data-plane operations. It is populated only when a diagnostic setting on the blob service sends logs to Log Analytics. Blob deletions are not in the Activity log.

q: On 5 November you change this policy's Expiry to 2026-11-10. What happens to SAS tokens that reference it?
opts: Nothing; existing tokens keep the original expiry
They now expire on 10 November (the change applies within about 30 seconds)
They are revoked immediately
They must be regenerated before the change applies
exp: SAS tokens linked to a stored access policy take their constraints from the policy, so changing the policy changes every linked token.

code:
Account st-std (StorageV2, Standard_LRS)
Name   QuotaGiB  AccessTier            EnabledProtocols
docs   100       TransactionOptimized  SMB

Account st-prem (FileStorage, Premium_LRS)
Name   QuotaGiB  AccessTier  EnabledProtocols
linux  1024      Premium     NFS
q: Review the shares in two storage accounts. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: The "linux" share is in a FileStorage (premium) account
Linux clients can mount "docs" over NFS
Windows clients can mount "docs" over SMB
The "docs" quota can grow past 5 TiB without enabling large file shares
exp: NFS shares exist only on premium FileStorage accounts. "docs" is an SMB share. Standard shares are limited to 5 TiB unless large file shares are enabled.

code:
az storage blob generate-sas --account-name st1 -c docs -n a.pdf \
  --permissions r --expiry 2026-11-20 \
  --auth-mode login --as-user
q: What kind of SAS does this command create?
opts: An account SAS signed with the account key
A service SAS signed with the account key
A user delegation SAS signed with Microsoft Entra credentials, valid for at most 7 days
A stored access policy
exp: --auth-mode login with --as-user creates a user delegation SAS. Its user delegation key is valid for up to 7 days.
